header.running_head: Getting Annoyed for the Sake of One's Elders

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) hits Two Men for their Insolence Towards Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once saw a man's garment hanging below his ankles, he told him to lift it up. The man retorted, "What about you, O Abdullaah bin Mas'ood? You also lift up your garment higher." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "I am not like you. My calves are extremely thin and I lead people in salaah (therefore if I lift my garment too high, people would be repulsed)." When news of this incident reached Hadhrat Umar (RA), he hit the man saying, "Do you backchat Ibn Mas'ood (RA)?"[^1]

Hadhrat Alaa reports from his teachers that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was once standing by the home of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) in Madinah, watching it being built when a man from the Quraysh remarked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Let someone else (like the owner) do this work for you." Hadhrat Umar (RA) grabbed hold of a brick and hurled it at the man saying, "Do you wish to make me dislike Ibn Mas'ood?"[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hits a Man for the Sake of Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that because Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) owed something to a certain man, the man took an oath against her. For this, Hadhrat Umar (RA) had the man lashed thirty stripes, causing his skin to be cut and to become swollen.[^3]
Hadhrat Ali (RA) Expresses the Intention to Execute Ibn Saba for Regarding him to be Superior to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Ummu Moosa reports that when the news reached Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Ibn Saba claimed that he (Hadhrat Ali (RA)) was superior to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) expressed the wish to have Ibn Saba executed. Someone remarked, "Will you execute a man for merely showing respect to you and for regarding you to be an esteemed person?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) then said, "Alright then (he need not be executed). However, he should never be allowed to live in the town where I reside."[^4]
